You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the test does:
  - It creates a directory entry named "föö/" (non-ASCII and ends with a slash), enables addPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames, and calls TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry on it.

- How putArchiveEntry handles this:
  - In TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry (lines 262–330), since addPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames is true and the entry name contains non-ASCII, it adds a PAX header key "path" with the original entry name (lines 302–305) and then calls writePaxHeaders(entryName, headers) (line 314).

- How the PAX header entry is constructed:
  - In writePaxHeaders (lines 454–491), the PAX header entry name is built as:
    name = "./PaxHeaders.X/" + stripTo7Bits(entryName) (lines 456–461).
  - For a directory name, entryName ends with "/", so name will also end with "/". The code even comments that TarEntry’s constructor would think this is a directory (lines 457–459), but it only truncates overly long names; it does not remove a trailing slash. Thus for short names like "föö/", the trailing slash remains.

- Why this causes the failure:
  - The PAX header entry is created with new TarArchiveEntry(name, LF_PAX_EXTENDED_HEADER_LC) (lines 462–464). The constructor TarArchiveEntry(String) it delegates to sets directory attributes if name endsWith("/") (lines 224–242, notably 228–235).
  - Even though the linkFlag is later set to LF_PAX_EXTENDED_HEADER_LC, TarArchiveEntry.isDirectory() returns true if getName().endsWith("/") (lines 724–737, especially 733–735). So this PAX entry is considered a directory.
  - writePaxHeaders computes the PAX data, sets pex.setSize(data.length) (line 487), then calls putArchiveEntry(pex) and write(data) (lines 488–490).
  - Inside putArchiveEntry, because entry.isDirectory() is true, currSize is set to 0 (lines 323–327). When write(data) is called, TarArchiveOutputStream.write checks (currBytes + numToWrite) > currSize and throws:
    "request to write '...' bytes exceeds size in header of '0' bytes for entry '...'" (lines 384–391).

- Relation to the current bug report:
  - The bug report’s exception matches exactly this path: when writing PAX headers for a directory (especially with long names, but also for non-ASCII names), the generated PAX header entry name ends with a slash, making it look like a directory with zero size. Writing the PAX header data then fails with the same IOException. The code even acknowledges the risk but only truncates length; it does not guard against trailing slashes.

- Root cause:
  - TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders constructs a PAX header entry name that may end with a trailing slash if the original entry name denotes a directory. Because TarArchiveEntry.isDirectory() treats any name ending with "/" as a directory, the PAX header entry is treated as size 0, and writing its data fails.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
